strengths: Slides 2–7 sustain a clear line/movement/texture editorial system rather than applying an arbitrary fashion skin.
Slide 3 uses front and three-quarter views to clarify how the fringe and face-framing layers behave, while slides 6 and 7 pair silhouette views with useful texture or construction details.
The casting and hairstyle range is notably broad: bob, fringe, pixie, shag, natural curls, and braids are represented across different hair textures and skin tones.
Typography, warm-neutral photography, burgundy rules, folios, and alternating compositions remain coherent without becoming mechanically repetitive.

issues.evidence: The cover visibly says, "Replace with approved salon photography and service names before publishing." This is draft-production instruction, not client-facing lookbook copy.
issues.fix: Replace the instruction with a salon name, season or collection date, and a concise editorial introduction. Use approved salon work before presenting this as the salon's latest work.

issues.evidence: Every slide identifies the images as "AI concept imagery — not salon work." The disclosure is honest, but the deck therefore does not yet fulfill the request for a lookbook of "our salon's" hairstyles.
issues.fix: Treat this as a concept template until authentic portfolio photography is inserted; retain only a discreet disclosure if concept imagery remains.

issues.evidence: The closing page reduces the collection to four small, widely separated thumbnails and ends with a generic stylist statement. It omits the salon identity, booking path, location, or a strong final full-bleed look.
issues.fix: Finish with one decisive hero image plus salon branding and a concrete consultation or booking action.

issues.evidence: The single profile crop communicates the pixie silhouette but does not show enough of the crown or rear shape to substantiate the caption's detailed claims about tapered nape and piece-by-piece separation.
issues.fix: Add a small rear or crown detail, as successfully done for texture on slides 6 and 7.

A.signatureMoment: Slide 6: the large natural-texture portrait beside a tight curl detail makes both the rounded silhouette and curl definition immediately legible.

strengths: Slide 2 is an effective fashion-editorial profile: the bob perimeter is large, unobstructed, and directly supports the caption.
Slides 6 and 7 provide strong hairstyle visibility and clean magazine hierarchy; the halo silhouette and braided low knot are easy to understand.
Slide 8 translates line, movement, and texture into a simple three-reference consultation device.
The neutral palette and restrained serif typography are visually consistent, with no visible clipping in the supplied renders despite the overflow report.

issues.evidence: The cover includes the visible draft instruction, "Replace with current salon photography and approved service names before publishing," and labels the work as concept imagery rather than salon work.
issues.fix: Remove production instructions and publish only after replacing the concept images and names with approved salon material.

issues.evidence: The opening hero is dominated by a woman in a wedding dress crossing an architectural interior; the hairstyle is small and secondary. It introduces a bridal-fashion story rather than a salon hairstyle lookbook.
issues.fix: Open with a tightly framed, unmistakable hair hero that establishes the collection's strongest cut or texture.

issues.evidence: The image for "The Air Cut" prominently shows a shaved side and swept-back or tied hair, while the copy describes airy crown length and a shifting short-hair silhouette. The visible hairstyle does not convincingly demonstrate the stated cut.
issues.fix: Select a model showing the described tapered nape, separated crown layers, and complete silhouette, or rewrite the service description to match the undercut image.

issues.evidence: Two different models and visibly different hair lengths are presented under one "Soft Shag" label. The left image reads as a short crop, while the right shows a longer tousled style, so the pair does not function as complementary views of one look.
issues.fix: Use front and movement views of the same haircut, or clearly label the images as two variations.

issues.evidence: The middle reference repeats the bridal woman from slide 1, extending the wedding-editorial motif and weakening the claim that this is the salon's latest hairstyle collection.
issues.fix: Replace it with a close hairstyle reference from the collection and add salon-specific booking information.

issues.evidence: The body copy and disclosure sit relatively small within a large empty column, making the page feel less resolved for projection than the stronger image-led pages.
issues.fix: Increase body size slightly and tighten the relationship among heading, rule, caption, and footer.

B.signatureMoment: Slide 7: the braided low knot fills the background while a restrained white caption card preserves detail visibility and editorial polish.

result.reason: I would give the user A, but only as the stronger draft: both decks fail the readiness gate because visible replacement instructions remain and neither presents authentic salon work. A wins in either presentation order because its photographs consistently prioritize hair, its captions align more closely with the visible styles, its casting is more inclusive, and its line/movement/texture structure is realized through useful multi-view layouts. B repeatedly drifts into bridal-fashion imagery and has substantive image-to-caption conflicts on slides 4 and 5. Route identity is not supplied, so the "original arm" cannot be identified; among the observed outputs, A's additional layout variation earns its complexity, whereas B's variation sometimes obscures the hairstyle. A exceeds competent default quality modestly through its tailored visual system, but the draft copy and weak closing prevent exceptional status.
result.whatWouldMakeWinnerExceptional: Replace every concept image with cohesive, authentic salon portfolio photography while preserving A's multi-angle editorial system, then add salon branding, service names, seasonal context, and a decisive full-bleed booking close.
